findings.detail: The implementation corrupts precomputed dense item embeddings with elementwise feature dropout, not stochastic views of available item metadata encoded by the text encoder. Thus the uncertainty being estimated is vector-coordinate dropout variance, not the specified metadata-view uncertainty. The comment confirms metadata text is absent. This changes the central mechanism rather than merely its implementation detail.
findings.reproduction: Inspect the input loading at lines 139-160 and 233-240: it loads sentence_t5.npy rows and never loads text or invokes an encoder f on text; the only corruption is the Bernoulli mask at lines 308-310.
findings.correction: Generate M independent dropout-corrupted views from each training item's available metadata and run the intended text encoder on each view; if only cached vectors are in scope, explicitly provide corresponding independently generated metadata-view embeddings rather than feature-mask approximations.

findings.detail: The specified agreement regularizer is the variance-weighted hard per-level code disagreement. The implementation returns that hard value in the forward pass but adds a latent squared-distance surrogate gradient. This is an additional optimization mechanism: even when the discrete code disagreement is zero, the surrogate drives views' encoded vectors together. It is not the stated objective, though it avoids the zero-gradient problem of a purely discrete penalty.
findings.reproduction: For two views with identical token tuples but distinct encoded vectors, `hard` is zero while `soft` is positive; line 33 returns zero forward value with gradient from `soft`.
findings.correction: Use a documented differentiable estimator explicitly approved as part of the design, or implement the specified objective and choose a deliberate gradient estimator whose forward and gradient behavior is separately controlled and tested.

findings.detail: The distributed codebook initialization is mismatched across ranks and deadlocks. Rank 0 enters `raw_module.init_codebook`, whose VQLayer.init_codebook calls `distributed.broadcast` at layers.py:143; nonzero ranks skip initialization and enter `dist.barrier()` instead. These ranks therefore execute different collectives in the same process group.
findings.reproduction: Launch the configured 4-rank torchrun path with RANK/LOCAL_RANK set. After rank 0 finishes KMeans it waits in broadcast while ranks 1-3 wait in barrier; none can progress. This occurs before the first training batch.
findings.correction: Have every rank enter codebook initialization in the same layer/order so the broadcast has matching participants, or compute centers on rank 0 and broadcast them with all ranks explicitly participating in that same broadcast before any barrier.

findings.detail: The trainer entry point is bound to absolute paths under `/home/wlia0047/ar57/wenyu/GeneRec`, while this checkout is `/fs04/ar57/wenyu/GeneRec`; consequently the real entry point cannot load its configured training inputs here, and its output paths are outside this tree. The existence/format of the claimed frozen data files at those hardcoded locations is not established by this tree.
findings.reproduction: Run `python train_rqvae.py` in the supplied checkout: the first `load_embeddings(EMBEDDING_FILE)` attempts `/home/wlia0047/.../sentence_t5.npy`; that path is not the checkout path. Even if run in the original host, missing either configured file raises immediately.
findings.correction: Bind the trainer to the project's canonical frozen-data paths (or a verified configuration mechanism) and validate both input files and item-row mapping before launching training.
